english: Husband, how many men will come to the feast? Ten men will come, and their wives too. Is there much mead in the house? There is not much. Go to your sister; there is mead in her house. I shall go, and she will give it, for she cherishes me. Go quickly; the guests are coming in the evening.

english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: Wake up, friend! The guests are going to their homes. Where am I? Why is it getting dark? Night has come; you slept beside the door. My head is heavy, and my mouth is dry. Do you want mead? I do not want it; give me water! I am bringing you water; then go and lie down.

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: The king gave you a horse, and to me he gave nothing. I told the fame of his lineage; you told of his mead. His mead is good! A king loves his own fame. Then early in the morning I shall sing of his great fame. Sing it, and he will give you an ox. I want a horse!

english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

english: Guest, you have eaten and drunk. Now sing us a song! My voice is not sweet; ask another man! The whole house is listening. Sing, and I shall give you a gift. What shall I sing? Sing the song of the hero who slew the serpent. I shall sing it. Listen, men!

english: Mother, who is that stranger at the hearth? I do not know; he arrived in the evening. Why did you not ask his name? A guest eats and is sated; then we ask him. And if he is an enemy? Sky protects every guest. Then I shall give him mead. Give it, and listen to his words.

english: Brother, the ox is dead. How shall we divide the meat? We shall cut off the thighs for the gods. We shall burn them in the fire, and the smoke will go up. And what will the guests receive? The guests will receive the fat meat, and the dogs will get the bones. The dogs will rejoice! They will rejoice. Now hand me the knife.

english: King, my share is small. Why do you say this? Every man received his own share. That man received the thigh, and I received a bone! He slew the boar. If you slay a boar, you too will receive the thigh. Then I shall go out early and hunt. Go, and may Perkunos guard you!

english: Husband, where shall the old men sit? Seat them near the fire, for old bones are cold. And the young men? The young men will sit near the door; they sing, and they fight. And where shall I sit? You will sit beside me, woman, and pour the mead. I shall pour it.

english: Father, why did you pour mead into the fire? Fire carries it to the gods. Then they rejoice and give us cattle and children. Do they drink mead? They drink it, and they love the smoke of the meat. May I pour for Fire? Pour, my son, and praise Father Sky!

english: Brother, that guest has devoured a sheep! And two horns of mead have gone into his belly. Now he wants the pig. Give him the pig, or he will eat us up! Where does that food go? Into his belly, which is bigger than a ship.

english: Woman, the barley has grown, and the year was good. Then let us make a feast for Perkunos, who rained on the fields. What shall we give him? A he-goat and beer. The god will receive the fat and the bones; the meat will be ours. Then he will be angry. He is not angry; the smoke is sweet to him.

english: Master, I have filled myself, and I am satisfied. Now tell me: from which village have you come? From the village of the river. Was the road long? It was long, and wolves followed me. You are bold. Lie here this night; early in the morning my son will lead you.

english: Grandmother, how do you make mead? I put honey into water and set the pot near the fire. Then it becomes tasty. May I sip it? When you are a bride, you will sip it at your own feast. Then may I soon be a bride! You are clever, child.

english: Grandmother, tell me the story of the feast of the gods. Father Sky prepared a great feast. The gods came, and they drank mead from cups of gold. Did they devour meat? They devoured the meat of a hundred cows, and Fire brought it to them. Do the gods still eat at our feasts? They eat; so we give the first share to Fire. Then I myself shall give him my porridge.

english: Mother, my head is in pain. Yesterday you drank much beer at the feast. I did not drink much; the cup was small. You filled it three times, and then you lay down under the table. Did anyone see me? The whole village saw you, and the young men laughed. I shall not drink again! You said that last year too.

english: Child, the cup has not reached me. I am carrying it around; now the men are sipping. The women are thirsty, and the men are drunk! Grandmother, the cup will come to you soon. May it be full when it comes! I myself shall fill it for you.

english: Master, I have spilled the wine! Where did you spill it? On the ground. Then Mother Earth sipped it; she was thirsty. Are you not angry? I am not angry; fill the cup again, and do not spill it! I shall not spill it again.

english: Grandfather, whom do we honour at this feast? We honour Dawn, the daughter of Sky. Why do we honour Dawn? In winter the nights are cold, and Dawn brings back the sun. Will you chant a hymn to her? I shall chant; you, pour the milk into the fire. I shall pour it, grandfather.

english: Mistress, I have come from the field. Is there meat for me? The guests have eaten up everything. Even the bones? The dogs took the bones; I hid meat for you in the pot. You are dear to me! Eat it quickly, or the boys will smell it.

english: Grandmother, your husband died last year. On this day we shall make a feast for him, and our kin will come. Will his spirit be with us? We shall place his share by the hearth, and in the night his spirit will come. He is gone, and my heart is sad. Sing his hymn at the feast; may his fame be great.

english: Elder, that man threatened me; I shall strike him! Do not fight at the feast, young man. Fire sees you. He seized my share of the meat! Then early in the morning he will give you two thighs, or he will pay a penalty. Two thighs? Then I shall not strike that man. Sit, and rejoice.

english: Lady, I am an orphan, and I am hungry. Come in, child, and sit down here. The guests have eaten; still, meat and barley are in the cauldron. May the gods give you good things! Eat this porridge and milk. Where is your mother? She died in the winter. Then stay with us; we shall feed you.
